title: a core that holds the history is the one that answers what is in it
asserts: a core that advertises `sessionSearch` answers `searchSessions` from its own store, over the whole history rather than over whatever a client happens to have seen. That is the half no client index can supply: a desktop mirror learns a session's bytes by attaching to it, so searching there matched the title of every session and the text of only the ones that Mac had opened - 508 of 857 sessions on the real pair against the 772 the daemon can answer for, measured 2026-09-17 (juancode-rz4c). The corpus is what was SAID: this drives a turn into the CLI's own transcript, never attaches a second client to it, and then asks a connection that has seen none of it. The `requestId` comes back unchanged, because a search box has a frame per keystroke in flight and the answers are not ordered.

steps.note: the fake agent writes this turn into claude's own jsonl, which is what a session's history is made of; the pty bytes it also prints are a different plane
a core's first bind attempt lands on the spawn banner, before this turn's file exists, so it backs off for BIND_RETRY; this outlasts that back-off
a bound transcript is only polled for a session that has produced output
one pump tick plus room, so the turn has landed in the store the search reads
the client this scenario is about: it was not connected for any of the above, so the turn is history it was never told
a session b never saw created, found by a word only its transcript holds
a word nothing said, to prove the answer is a search and not the session list
